newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech Union Banka moves to protect Slovak Ekoagro.
newsitem.headline: Czech Union Banka moves to protect Slovak Ekoagro.

text.p: Czech Union Banka a.s. on Tuesday said it was closing its Ekoagrobanka Slovak branches temporarily to protect deposits after the Slovak central bank revoked its banking licence on Sunday.

Union Banka, which took majority control of Ekoagrobanka after it had been under forced administration of the Czech central bank since January, said it would appeal against the National Bank of Slovakia's (NBS) move, calling it unjustified.
It also said that it was negotiating with undisclosed partners to sell the Slovak unit.
Union Banka said the forced administration at Ekoagrobanka remains, but is little more than a formality, which should end when the bank is re-entered into the business registry.

"The NBS has been regularly informed about all of the (recovery) steps taken and all its demands on the Slovak unit of Ekoagrobanka have been fulfilled in time and in to the required extent," a Union Banka statement said.
NBS officials were not immediately available for comment.
On Sunday, the NBS said it withdrew the Ekoagrobanka's licence because it had failed to show positive results in the recovery process after being placed under forced administration.
It then added on Monday that the move was a pre-emptive strike to keep any problems the Czech bank has had from entering the Slovak banking system.

The Union Banka statement added that it was forced to protect its deposits because the NBS informed the press of its decision in such a way that it could lead to a drop in confidence and a result in a run on the bank.
The statement added that all the deposits in Slovakia were fully covered and that the bank would fulfil all of its liabilities to clients.
